entries.headline: The design keeps task context separate from working files

intent.text: Keep the task's recorded context alongside your draft without changing your chosen source, opening a file or sending an agent command.

outcome.text: The recorded design gives a task its own read-only, revision-labelled section. Git records the design and base changes as merged.

decision.text: Recommendation: check the later UI and core milestones before treating the older design status as a delivery summary.

caveats: The design specifies exact commit/blob identity and core revalidation, separate from editable instructions and independently captured source.
Its status paragraph still describes the earlier D3-only stage, when attached Prepare was unavailable; it is not an aggregate delivery status.
The artifact is a supplied paraphrase. Git records changed document, protocol, core and test paths, not proof of correct behavior.
Card order presents a progression, not proof of causal dependencies.

entries.headline: Reported task attachment leaves the chosen source unchanged

intent.text: Add, replace or remove a task deliberately while keeping control of the source used by the draft.

outcome.text: D5 reports that attaching a task kept the draft's chosen source and unsaved work intact. Git records the attachment UI merge.

decision.text: Recommendation: use this record to understand task attachment; consult the core milestone before assessing preparation of a task-backed draft.

caveats: D5 reports Append/Replace/Cancel/Remove controls, rejection of stale proposals and invalidation of preparation after accepted changes.
Packaged checks at 100%/150%, retained dirty state and zero renderer exceptions are D5's attributed report, not independently rerun here.
At this milestone, attached Prepare returned UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL. Later merges do not change that historical result.

entries.headline: Core preparation was reported to check the exact task version

intent.text: Keep a prepared draft tied to the selected task version, with its source and configuration checked separately.

outcome.text: D4 reports that core loaded and checked the selected task text. That initial recap preceded peer clearance; Git separately records the later core merge.

decision.text: Recommendation: use the merge record for what landed, and keep these preparation results separate from claims about production agent launch.

caveats: D4 reports Git/YAML checks of task identity, commit and blob, bounded canonical text, and independent revalidation of metadata, source and configuration.
Cancellation and shutdown drain, 40-second task Prepare and unchanged five-second ordinary/launch uncertainty are reported results, not checks rerun here.

The initial recap was held before peer clearance. The bundle does not explain how that was resolved; the later merge records changed resolver, core and test paths, not the causal story or correctness.
Production launch remained ADAPTER_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE in the report; deterministic admission/history is not production model execution.

entries.headline: Recorded checks found 81 history records intact after recovery

intent.text: Check that task-run history survives recovery and closing, while distinguishing real task data from simulated agent output.

outcome.text: D6 and ROOT report that all 81 history records stayed unchanged through recovery and closing, with owned processes cleaned up. Git separately records the integration merge.

decision.text: Recommendation: keep these results as recorded rehearsal evidence, and keep tracking the reported timeout and resize warning; a quiet run does not prove either is fixed.

caveats: ROOT's imported check records equal pre/post hashes, two core generations, no replayed commands and owned PIDs absent. Its build/test and lifecycle verification was not rerun by Journal.
Git/Ditz task metadata and the resolver were real; the admitted output was deterministic, not live agents.
The production proof recorded modelTurns=0; the separate rehearsal recorded fixtureOnly=true and externalAgentProcesses=0.
The resize warning remained nonblocking under reported user disposition; the original topology timeout also remained open.
Generator provenance identifies this supervised authoring run only. The UI did not execute a model.
